Lessons and exercises: team feedback

Notes collected on the current screens, grouped as to review, good points and to think about. Each item is one piece of feedback by Anais or Victor with a comment by Bastian and a number that identifies it on the whole page. The items are in four sections: clarification needed, not implemented yet, already implemented in main (status of 2026-10-14), and discarded.

#28 MAIN POINTS Lesson length from A1 to C2 Feedback by Endrit and Bastian
Should lessons get longer from A1 to C2? And is the current length of vocabulary lessons enough to teach the number of words each level requires?
OPEN QUESTIONS
  • Do we want lessons to get longer from A1 to C2, or does every lesson stay at about 15 minutes?
  • Is the current length of vocabulary lessons (8–9 words, 14–15 minutes, D14) enough to reach the number of words each level requires? If not: more words per lesson, or more lessons per level?
FROM THE READING REVIEW (PR #95)

Bastian: “so far I set every lesson to 15min, but I like advancing from A1 to C2. let's discuss this tonight at 22”

Endrit: “With the page rules now in the spec, A1 takes about 8 minutes and C2 about 14, so every level stays within the 15-minute rule. Whether B2–C2 may take longer is listed as an open point for the team (P5-05, #103)”

#14 GRAMMAR Screen 1 · Singular Subject Pronouns Feedback by Anais
SCREEN 1
Singular Subject Pronouns
Read the explanation and the examples
TO REVIEW
  • Could be more visual
  • Take point by point, not the subject
MOCKUP
Visual intro and a side bar by point: see the side bar mockup "Grammar: Singular Subject Pronouns" below.

Same content as the current screens, with a side bar listing the points of the lesson or the pages of the exam.

COMMENT BASTIAN
The sidebar is implemented, but the introduction does not look like this mockup. The introduction will be AI-generated for every lesson: how would you get a visual like this with a JSON lesson format? Would you let the AI generate HTML freely (dangerous), or how would you restrict it?
#10 VOCABULARY Screen 2 · Type the right word (accent) Feedback by Anais
SCREEN 2
Type the right word (accent)
Choose the right word and type it
TO REVIEW
  • Feels like an old website…
  • Sentence must be on top and more clear
  • Sentence asking for the accent must be in the native language, not the learning language
GOOD POINTS
  • Good to have answers and gender
  • Good to have a hint
  • Misspelling the good answer does not make the answer false
TO THINK ABOUT
  • Example: "What is the accent name in the word: café (é)?"
  • UX recommendation: should pressing Enter validate the answer?
  • Writing the answer is a good exercise, but it must be balanced with other types of exercise (choose the right answer by clicking it)
COMMENT BASTIAN
Please supply an actual mockup of how you would change it, and say what needs to be changed so that it does not look like an old website.

#24 ALL LESSONS Listen to the sentences with a speaker Feedback by Victor
I would add maybe option to listen the sentenses by clicking on speaker in all lessons, it helps to understand the pronounciation of the sentenses, espetially when you in A1 and already in very first lessons you get examples of full sentences in french.
COMMENT BASTIAN
Partly: vocabulary flashcards and function lessons already have a speaker for their example sentences. Grammar explanations and examples, and the vocabulary introduction, have no audio yet. P6-02.
#25 VOCABULARY Listening: skip or replace when the learner cannot listen Feedback by Victor
In “Listen and choose the word you hear.” I would give some option not to listen when user cannot afford it. Maybe just skip it with “skip” button. Maybe to replace it with equivalent excercise that doesn't require listening but uses the same word, so that we still can eval it.
COMMENT BASTIAN
Partly: a “Skip listening task” button exists only when no French voice is installed, and a skipped task is left out of the score. Skipping by choice, or an equivalent exercise without audio for the same word, is open in P6-02.

3. Already implemented (10)

In main, on branch P06-00, or nothing to change.

#1 MAIN POINTS Lessons must be shorter Feedback by Anais and Victor
Anais: Lessons must be shorter.
Victor: Lesson too long.
COMMENT BASTIAN
Implemented on branch P06-00 (P6-02): every lesson is shorter, with the outlines unchanged. Vocabulary: 8–9 words per lesson (14–15 min). Grammar: fewer practice and exam items (15 min). Functions: 4 expressions instead of 8, with every exercise type kept (16–17 min). The generator now plans lessons of at most 15 minutes.
#3 MAIN POINTS 0/100 during introduction and theory Feedback by Anais
0/100 is not relevant for the user: it does not make sense to see it while having introduction and theory.
COMMENT BASTIAN
Done on branch P06-00: the session header shows no score on pages without answers (introduction, theory, flashcards, exam info, feedback placeholder). The progress bar and percentage stay.
#5 SIDE BAR MOCKUP V2 · Vertical timeline Feedback by Anais

Same content as the current screens, with a side bar listing the points of the lesson or the pages of the exam.

COMMENT BASTIAN
Done in main, with changes: P6-01 (#69, PR #87) built a V2 timeline, but not as drawn. Done points keep their number in a filled circle instead of a tick; there is no Previous button (no way back to earlier points) and no segmented bar above the content. Since P06-00 the header shows no score on theory pages.
#6 SIDE BAR MOCKUP Exam in progress: time limit display Feedback by Anais

Same content as the current screens, with a side bar listing the points of the lesson or the pages of the exam.

COMMENT BASTIAN
Implemented on branch P06-00 (P6-02): the exam page shows a “Time left” box to the right of the heading, with the time in large digits and a bar of the time remaining on the page; in the last 10 seconds it turns red. Since P6-01 the sidebar lists the exam pages with their time limits.
#26 SIDE BAR MOCKUP Exam in progress: exam task display Feedback by Anais

Same content as the current screens, with a side bar listing the points of the lesson or the pages of the exam.

COMMENT BASTIAN
Implemented on branch P06-00 (P6-02): exam pages with more than one typed answer (vocabulary translation and dictation, grammar typed gaps, function translation) show every task as a numbered card, the task on the left and the field on the right (stacked on phones); the function exam dialogue keeps its layout. The first field takes the cursor.
